problemStatement.formal: theorem hurwitz_only_if (N : Type*) [NormedDivisionAlgebra N] : Module.finrank ℝ N ∈ ({1, 2, 4, 8} : Set ℕ) := by sorry
problemStatement.plain: Can hurwitz_only_if (the hard direction of Hurwitz's theorem) be proved via Clifford algebra theory and the representation of norm-preserving multiplications? The classical argument uses Radon-Hurwitz numbers: a normed division algebra of dimension n requires Cl(n-1) to have a real representation of dimension n, which forces n ∈ {1,2,4,8}.
whyMatters: Hurwitz's theorem is a landmark result in algebra — fully machine-checked proof is significant
The Clifford algebra approach is the most conceptual proof
Connects to K-theory, Bott periodicity, and the Hopf invariant one problem
